AI.motivation: Traditional LLM-driven bioinformatics systems treat planning, tool use, and execution as transient interactions, which breaks traceability for long-horizon analyses. There is a need to tie conclusions to data, computations, and intermediate evidence through persistent, governed workflows.
AI.method: Bioinfoysis introduces a persistent analysis run where a global planner maintains an executable checklist and performs step-wise replanning via structured handoffs that bind results to agents, steps, and plans. A controlled runtime validates scripts, tables, and figures before downstream use. The system leverages role-specific context, memory, and governance for reliable long-horizon execution. Evaluation spans BixBench and two tracks of LAB-Bench 2, across four LLMs.
AI.result: On BixBench, Bioinfoysis achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 82.4%. Across SeqQA2 and DbQA2, average accuracy improves from 27.81% to 64.13% and from 3.13% to 31.25%, respectively, when using four underlying LLMs.
AI.conclusion: Reliability in bioinformatics automation hinges on governance of planning, memory, and evidence flow, not just model capability. Bioinfoysis could stimulate community development; a demo is available at the provided URL.

title: It's the Problem, Not the Path: Budget and Difficulty Confounds in LLM Reasoning Trajectories
comment: 25 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Also available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22261107. Code and pre-registered protocols: https://github.com/bulutyigit/problem-not-path
summary: Reasoning traces of large language models are widely read as containing "breakthrough" moments and early-legible fates. Both readings rest on measurements missing a counterfactual control at the level of the claim; we supply both controls. First, a restart-controlled truncation probe separates when a solution fits the continuation budget from when a prefix carries value that fresh computation cannot buy, comparing per-anchor continuation solve rates against from-scratch restart curves at matched total generated-token budget. Applied to 178 problem-model cells (89 MATH problems x two small open models, an outcome-blind but difficulty-targeted cohort), exactly 1 of 178 cells survives as prefix-limited; restart dose-response separates a compute-starved model from a capability-limited one; and wherever the matched budget lies inside the restart grid, continuing the model's own prefix beats restarting (9 of 9) -- predominantly compute compression rather than expanded reachability. Second, a pre-registered, difficulty-controlled test finds no detectable outcome information in early-window internal signals beyond a problem-difficulty baseline, and two generation-free analyses of public corpora show why this control is needed: a trace-blind difficulty proxy reaches AUROC 0.873 on 192K DeepSeek-R1 generations -- inside the published probe range -- and a closely matched reconstruction of the closest published early-window positive recovers a comparable pooled result (0.849) while within problem it is statistically indistinguishable from chance at all ten anchors (0.496 at t=4); a post-hoc within-targeted probe finds only a small average residual, concentrated in three low-failure problems. High pooled probe AUROCs cannot by themselves establish within-attempt information; a question-only baseline or within-problem evaluation is required.

AI.tldr: Counterfactual controls show most LLM 'breakthrough' signals arise from compute budgets, not emergent reasoning; early signals lack robust information about outcomes.
AI.motivation: Debunk the interpretation that early internal signals in LLM reasoning reveal real cognitive breakthroughs. Introduce restart-controlled truncation probes and difficulty-controlled tests, plus generation-free analyses, to isolate budget effects from genuine capability.
AI.method: 1) Restart-controlled truncation probe across 178 problem-model cells comparing per-anchor continuation vs from-scratch budgets; 2) Pre-registered, difficulty-controlled test of early-window signals; 3) Generation-free analyses of public corpora to illustrate the need for controls; 4) Post-hoc within-targeted probe for residual effects.
AI.result: Only 1/178 cells shows prefix-limited advantage; restart dose-response separates compute-starved vs capability-limited models; when budgets match, continuing the prefix beats restarting in 9/9 cases (mainly due to compute compression). Difficulty-controlled test finds no detectable outcome information beyond problem difficulty; two generation-free analyses show high AUROCs driven by a difficulty proxy; within-problem results are near chance; post-hoc probe finds small residuals in a few low-failure problems.
AI.conclusion: High AUROCs do not prove within-attempt knowledge; without proper controls, apparent breakthroughs overstate LLM reasoning capabilities. Required: a question-only baseline or within-problem evaluation to claim genuine within-attempt information.

title: DropClick: Semi-Automated One-Click Segmentation for Agricultural Robotic Data
summary: Labelling vision datasets, especially for segmentation tasks, is a laborious and costly process that stymies novel developments in agricultural robotics. In this paper, we present DropClick, a click-guided segmentation tool that simplifies the annotation process. Our system utilises single-click inputs on objects to generate pseudo-labels, which can replace manual annotations. DropClick stands out as it is a semi-automated approach and does not require a click for every object in the scene. It can therefore further reduce the required amount of user input drastically. We evaluate our method on two challenging agricultural robotic datasets, SB20 and BUP20 for plant and fruit segmentation, respectively. DropClick is first trained on a small subset of just 5 images from the original training data. This DropClick model can then be deployed as a one-click segmentation system and achieves comparable or higher performance than other one-click methods achieving an mIoU of 70.0 and 72.6 points, for SB20 and BUP20 respectively. DropClick then excels at maintaining high performance when clicks are not given (e.g. dropped); when 50% of the clicks are missing it still maintains an mIoU of 68.9 and 71.3 points, for SB20 and BUP20 respectively. We validate DropClick as a pseudo-labelling approach by taking its outputs to train a Mask2Former instance-based segmentation model in a semi-supervised manner. In this process, partially removing user input from DropClick yields similar high performance when compared to providing all clicks, at 70.1 vs 70.7 points AP50 for SB20 and no difference for BUP20 at 77.0 for both models; at the same time saving 46.3% of total input for SB20 and 31.9% for BUP20.

AI.tldr: DropClick is a semi-automated, click-guided segmentation tool that reduces annotation effort for agricultural datasets, achieving competitive one-click performance and robustness to missing clicks, and usable as pseudo-labels for semi-supervised training with Mask2Former.
AI.motivation: Annotation is a bottleneck for segmentation in agriculture; there is a need for efficient labeling methods to accelerate model development in agricultural robotics.
AI.method: Single-click inputs on objects generate pseudo-labels; trained on a small subset (as few as 5 images); deployed as a one-click segmentation system that can operate with partial input (clicks not required for every object); evaluated on SB20 (plants) and BUP20 (fruits); further used as pseudo-labels to train a Mask2Former instance segmentation model in a semi-supervised setting.
AI.result: One-click mIoU: 70.0 (SB20) and 72.6 (BUP20). With 50% missing clicks: 68.9 (SB20) and 71.3 (BUP20). As pseudo-labels for Mask2Former: AP50 70.1 vs 70.7 for SB20 (comparable); no difference for BUP20 at 77.0. Input savings: 46.3% (SB20) and 31.9% (BUP20).
AI.conclusion: DropClick reduces annotation effort while maintaining competitive performance, even with partial input; serves as an effective pseudo-label generator for semi-supervised segmentation in agricultural robotics.

title: Occlusion-Robust Multimodal Emotion Recognition in VR via Fusion of Facial Images and EMG
comment: Joint Proceedings of the ACM Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI) Workshops 2026
summary: Head-mounted displays (HMDs) fundamentally limit emotion recognition in virtual reality (VR): by occluding the upper face, they render conventional image-based facial expression analysis incomplete, particularly for applications requiring real-time affective assessment. We address this challenge by fusing lower-face video with facial electromyography (EMG) from the occluded upper face to classify seven emotional categories (six basic emotions plus neutral). We introduce a synchronized multimodal dataset from 20 participants, pairing lower-face video with seven-channel upper-face EMG elicited by validated emotion stimuli. Under subject-independent test, our proposed late-fusion architecture merging convolutional visual embeddings with RBF-kernel EMG representations achieves 51% macro-F1, outperforming both image-only (41%) and EMG-only (43%) baselines. These results demonstrate that upper-face EMG provides robust complementary information under HMD-induced visual occlusion and establish a foundation for multimodal emotion recognition in naturalistic VR environments. This approach facilitates affect-adaptive applications, including communication training and therapeutic interventions. The dataset will be shared upon request under an ethical-use agreement.

AI.tldr: Multimodal emotion recognition for HMD-based VR using lower-face video plus upper-face EMG; late fusion of conv visual embeddings and RBF-kernel EMG features yields 51% macro-F1 on seven emotions (six basic + neutral) in a 20-participant dataset, outperforming image-only (41%) and EMG-only (43%) baselines; dataset will be shared on request; supports affect-adaptive VR applications.
AI.motivation: HMDs occlude the upper face, limiting traditional image-based emotion recognition in VR; there is a need for robust, real-time affective assessment in naturalistic VR environments.
AI.method: Synchronized multimodal dataset from 20 participants: lower-face video + seven-channel upper-face EMG elicited by validated emotion stimuli. Seven emotion categories. Subject-independent evaluation. Late-fusion architecture combining convolutional visual embeddings with Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel EMG representations.
AI.result: Macro-F1 score of 0.51 in subject-independent tests, outperforming image-only baseline (0.41) and EMG-only baseline (0.43). Demonstrates complementary information from upper-face EMG under HMD occlusion.
AI.conclusion: Upper-face EMG provides robust complementary information for emotion recognition under VR-induced occlusion, enabling multimodal approaches in naturalistic VR and informing affect-adaptive applications; dataset available upon ethical-use request.

title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation
summary: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a key component for generating accurate and hallucination free answers using Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are improving at handling long context, but still suffer from "lost in the middle" problem. Thus, precise and accurate retrieval is important. Current retrievers chunk long context into length-based manageable chunks - in the process throwing away rich and informative semantic global structure in the corpus. We introduce a novel retrieval system STAIR that empowers an LLM to exploit global structure in a corpus such as a Table of Contents (ToC) to efficiently store and retrieve information from its model parameters. Our thorough and careful ablation studies with a finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI) system show that ToC helps build a low hallucination (less than 0.05%) generative Information Retrieval (IR) system and can generalize to examples where very few training samples are available. To further research in this novel direction of ToC based retrieval we release SearchTome - a diverse benchmark created from 18 books across 6 diverse domains to further research in this novel direction. STAIR achieves a high Recall@1 score of 82.6% on SearchTome as compared to DSI (76.9%), where the difference is found to be statistically significant. STAIR easily beats other strong baselines such as BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%) and out-of-the-box Mistral (13.8%).

AI.tldr: Introduces STAIR, a ToC-enabled retrieval system that uses global corpus structure to store/retrieve information via a Differentiable Search Index, achieving high low-hallucination IR and strong recall, and releasing SearchTome benchmark.
AI.motivation: Address the loss of global semantic structure when chunking long contexts for retrieval, leading to hallucinations and suboptimal accuracy in RAG; leverage a Table of Contents-style global structure to guide retrieval and parameter-based storage.
AI.method: Proposes STAIR with finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI); uses ToC as global guide; ablation studies; evaluates on SearchTome benchmark; compares with BM25, DPR, Mistral.
AI.result: Recall@1 82.6% on SearchTome vs 76.9% for DSI; outperforms BM25 59.5%, DPR 68.7%, Mistral 13.8%; hallucination rate <0.05%.
AI.conclusion: ToC-based retrieval with STAIR is effective for low-hallucination IR and generalizes to few-shot settings; Release of SearchTome to facilitate future research.

title: Guide, Not Bind: Why Defeasible Priors Fail in Augmented Lagrangian Causal Discovery
summary: Differentiable causal discovery methods increasingly encode expert priors as forbidden-edge constraints enforced by an Augmented Lagrangian (ALM) penalty, on the assumption that a data-adaptive relaxation mechanism will discount and eventually override a rule the data consistently contradicts. We show this design, which we call \emph{guide, not bind}, fails for two independent, precisely characterized reasons, and that directly repairing both restores it only partially. First, sequential penalty-ramping ALM suppresses a wrongly-forbidden true edge before any counterfactual check can detect it: we give three necessary conditions any adaptive relaxation must satisfy to avoid this (Proposition~\ref{prop:conditions}), prove that DADU---the natural relaxation rule this paper introduces as the object of study---violates all three (Corollary~\ref{cor:dadu_failure}), and confirm the failure across 3{,}072 training runs spanning graphs from 4 to 32 nodes, where a single wrong prior suppresses a true edge in 87--97\% of trials under DADU. Second, and independent of any fix to the mechanism, we prove in closed form that the standard correlation-matching objective ties a true edge and its reverse to an identical cost of exactly $2r^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tie}), not because the underlying equal-variance model is unidentifiable, but because normalizing to correlation discards exactly the variance information that would make it identifiable; covariance matching instead separates the two directions by a provable margin of at least $w_0^4$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:separation}).

AI.tldr: The abstract argues that guide-not-bind ALM-based priors in differentiable causal discovery fail: (1) a data-adaptive relaxation (DADU) suppresses true edges when a wrong prior is present, violating three necessary conditions for safe adaptation, with empirical failure across 3,072 runs on 4–32-node graphs; (2) correlation-matching ties a true edge and its reverse to identical cost 2r^2 due to losing variance information from normalization, while covariance matching separates directions by at least w0^4. Implications: rethink priors and prefer covariance-based objectives; improve theoretical guarantees for adaptive relaxations.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the efficacy of enforcing expert priors as forbidden edges via augmented Lagrangian penalties in differentiable causal discovery, and to test whether data-driven relaxation can override incorrect priors.
AI.method: Theoretically derive three necessary conditions for any adaptive relaxation to avoid suppressing true edges; prove DADU violates all three; provide a closed-form analysis showing correlation-matching ties directions and that covariance matching yields a provable separation; validate findings with extensive empirical experiments (3,072 training runs) on graphs with 4–32 nodes.
AI.result: DADU suppresses a wrongly-forbidden true edge in 87–97% of trials; correlation-matching yields identical cost for true edge and reverse (2r^2); covariance matching achieves a separation margin of at least w0^4.
AI.conclusion: The guide-not-bind strategy is inadequate for reliable causal discovery with priors. Repairs to the mechanism help only partially. One should prefer covariance-aware objectives and reassess the use of forbidden-edge priors, with attention to variance information and identifiability.

title: Drive-HWM: Hierarchical World Models for Dynamic-Latent Guided Autonomous Driving
summary: World models offer a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by predicting how traffic scenes may evolve and using such predictions to support action generation. However, existing approaches either separate future prediction from action generation or jointly predict them at the same temporal scale, making it difficult to simultaneously achieve long-horizon anticipation and responsive, observation-grounded decision making. We present Drive-HWM, a hierarchical slow--fast world modeling framework that organizes future representation prediction and action generation at complementary temporal scales. The slow world model predicts multi-step future representations to capture extended scene evolution. To explicitly model the abundant motion dynamics in driving environments, we introduce Dynamic-Aware Latents learned through optical-flow prediction. Guided by these future representations, the fast model uses a lightweight multimodal backbone and an autoregressive expert to jointly predict the next frame and the immediate action from the latest observation. Next-frame prediction encourages the fast model to capture imminent scene evolution, while one-step action generation allows decisions to be continuously updated as new observations arrive. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 demonstrate the strong driving performance of Drive-HWM. Comprehensive ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the hierarchical slow--fast design, dynamics-aware future representations, and joint next-frame and action prediction.

AI.tldr: Drive-HWM presents a hierarchical slow–fast world model for autonomous driving that decouples long-horizon future representation prediction from short-horizon action generation, using dynamic-aware latents via optical flow to capture motion and a fast autoregressive module to predict the next frame and immediate action.
AI.motivation: Address the gap between long-horizon scene evolution prediction and responsive, observation-grounded action in autonomous driving. Existing approaches struggle to achieve both due to either separate prediction or identical temporal scales.
AI.method: A hierarchical slow–fast framework: a slow world model predicting multi-step future representations; Dynamic-Aware Latents learned through optical-flow prediction to capture motion dynamics; a fast model with lightweight backbone and an autoregressive expert that jointly predicts the next frame and the immediate action from the latest observation; next-frame prediction guides imminent scene evolution, while one-step action enables continuous updates.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 show strong driving performance; comprehensive ablations confirm the effectiveness of the hierarchical slow–fast design, dynamics-aware latent representations, and joint next-frame and action prediction.
AI.conclusion: Drive-HWM effectively combines long-horizon foresight with responsive, observation-grounded control via a hierarchical slow–fast world model and dynamics-aware representations, offering improved driving performance and opportunities for further analysis and extension.

title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
summary:
We introduce Xiaomi-TabLDM, a tabular large data foundation model for classification and regression via in-context learning, which delivers superior prediction accuracy without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. Pretrained exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs), our model enables more flexible context utilization and more efficient capacity scaling.
  i) A new performance standard. Strong regression performance across benchmarks: Xiaomi-TabLDM ranks 1st on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO, demonstrating consistently strong regression performance across four complementary benchmark suites. Favorable performance--efficiency trade-off: Xiaomi-TabLDM combines strong predictive performance with substantially lower computational cost. For example, on TabArena regression, it achieves the second-highest Elo while using 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time than the top-ranked TabFM.
  ii) Large-scale synthetic pretraining. Xiaomi-TabLDM expands the coverage and diversity of synthetic tabular data used for pretraining. We also adopt a three-stage training strategy together with dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts, enabling Xiaomi-TabLDM to learn richer feature interactions and expert specialization across diverse tabular tasks.
  iii) Test-time scaling. Xiaomi-TabLDM further extends tabular prediction through test-time compute scaling, where allocating additional computation at inference time consistently improves predictive performance over the base model.

AI.tldr: Tabular LDM pretrained on synthetic SCM data achieves state-of-the-art regression with in-context learning and scalable inference, offering strong accuracy and significant efficiency gains without task-specific fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Address robust tabular prediction (classification/regression) without task-specific fine-tuning by leveraging synthetic data and scalable in-context learning; broaden coverage of feature interactions via SCM-based pretraining.
AI.method: Three-stage synthetic pretraining from structural causal models; dual-stream feature grouping; lightweight Attention Residual; sparse Mixture-of-Experts; in-context learning for predictions; test-time compute scaling to improve performance.
AI.result: Ranked 1st on OpenML-CTR23; 2nd in regression across TALENT, TabArena, BCCO; TabArena: 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time than top TabFM; achieves strong accuracy with favorable efficiency trade-offs; demonstrates improved prediction via test-time compute scaling.
AI.conclusion: Xiaomi-TabLDM shows that synthetic SCM-based pretraining plus in-context learning can yield strong tabular predictive performance with scalable inference and efficient training/prediction, enabling robust, non-finetuned tabular modeling.

title: Beyond Straightness: Non-Crossing Flow Matching via Quantile AlignTree Coupling
summary: The performance of Flow Matching largely depends on the quality of the coupling between the source and target distributions. However, independent coupling often leads to path crossings and local velocity ambiguity, while OT-based couplings typically incur high construction costs. To address this challenge, we propose Quantile AlignTree Flow Matching (QAT-FM), an efficient structured coupling strategy that constructs a hierarchical coupling between a Gaussian prior and the target data distribution via a quantile-aligned tree structure. QAT-FM constructs the coupling in $\mathcal{O}(Nd\log N)$ time and supports per-pair source sampling with $\mathcal{O}(d)$ complexity, enabling scalable training for large-scale high-dimensional generative tasks. Theoretically, we prove that the QAT coupling satisfies marginal consistency, induces non-crossing linear interpolation paths, and consistently improves path separation at intermediate times compared with independent coupling, thereby alleviating local velocity ambiguity. QAT-FM further extends naturally to conditional generation, enabling structured conditional coupling while preserving global Gaussian alignment. Experiments across diverse benchmark datasets demonstrate that QAT-FM achieves competitive generative performance while substantially reducing coupling construction cost.

AI.tldr: QAT-FM builds a hierarchical, quantile-aligned coupling between a Gaussian prior and target data, achieving O(N d log N) coupling construction with per-pair sampling O(d). It ensures marginal consistency, non-crossing interpolation paths, and improved path separation over independent couplings, enabling scalable conditional generation with competitive performance and lower cost.
AI.motivation: To address the drawbacks of independent couplings (path crossings and velocity ambiguity) and OT-based couplings (high cost) in Flow Matching by introducing an efficient, structured coupling that aligns quantiles through a tree structure.
AI.method: Construct a hierarchical, quantile-aligned tree that pairs Gaussian prior samples with target data, producing a coupling in O(N d log N) time. Enables per-pair source sampling with O(d) complexity. The approach yields marginally consistent, non-crossing interpolation paths and improved path separation. Extends naturally to conditional generation while preserving global Gaussian alignment.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation across diverse benchmarks shows competitive generative performance with substantially reduced coupling construction cost, validating scalability and effectiveness of the proposed coupling strategy.
AI.conclusion: QAT-FM provides an efficient, structured coupling for Flow Matching that preserves Gaussian alignment, reduces construction cost, supports conditional generation, and mitigates local velocity ambiguity through non-crossing interpolation paths and improved path separation.

title: GraFT: A Training-Free Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via 3D Scene Graphs
summary: 3D spatial reasoning underpins understanding and acting in the physical world, yet it remains unreliable in current multimodal large language models (MLLMs). These models falter at precise geometric measurement, at transforming between egocentric and allocentric viewpoints, and at grounding fine-grained appearance. The most common remedies fine-tune the model on large-scale curated spatial-reasoning datasets or attach dedicated encoders for 3D geometry, which typically couples the solution to costly supervision and a specific backbone. We instead introduce GraFT, a training-free framework that supplies the missing 3D structure through a compact, easily maintained 3D scene graph (3DSG). From this 3DSG, GraFT provides three spatial reasoning capabilities: (1) deterministic geometry through symbolic tools, (2) allocentric layout through a bird's-eye-view (BEV) rendering, and (3) visual-attribute grounding through task-relevant egocentric frames. On ScanQA, GraFT improves every metric over the same-backbone baseline, raising CIDEr by 27%. On VSI-Bench, GraFT improves frozen MLLMs by up to 65%, surpassing every proprietary and general-purpose open-source baseline, and several prominent fine-tuned spatial models.

AI.tldr: GraFT provides a training-free 3D reasoning layer for MLLMs via a compact 3D scene graph, enabling deterministic geometry, BEV allocentric layout, and egocentric grounding, boosting performance without retraining.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs struggle with precise geometry, viewpoint transformations, and fine-grained grounding; typical fixes rely on costly supervision or backbone-specific encoders, limiting generalization and efficiency.
AI.method: Introduce a lightweight 3D scene graph (3DSG) that supplies 3D structure at inference time. Use symbolic geometric tools for deterministic measurements, BEV rendering for allocentric layout, and task-relevant egocentric frames for grounding, all without training or backbone modification.
AI.result: On ScanQA, GraFT improves CIDEr by 27% over the same-backbone baseline; VSI-Bench: frozen MLLMs gain up to 65%, beating proprietary and open-source baselines and several fine-tuned spatial models.
AI.conclusion: A training-free, backbone-agnostic approach that leverages structured 3D priors to enhance 3D spatial reasoning in multimodal models, reducing dependency on data-intensive fine-tuning.

title: Text2Thermal: Physics-Aware Thermal Image Synthesis from Textual Priors
summary: Thermal infrared imaging offers reliable perception in darkness and adverse weather, but thermal datasets remain scarce, motivating extensive work on translating abundant RGB images into thermal. Such translation is fundamentally ill-posed as thermal appearance is governed by surface emissivity and object temperature, neither of which is observable in the visible spectrum, so a single RGB image is consistent with many valid thermal outputs. We argue that language offers a natural means of resolving this ambiguity, and propose Text2Thermal, a framework for physics-aware thermal image synthesis from textual priors. Rather than inferring the unobservable radiometric factors from RGB, we supply them explicitly through thermally grounded captions encoding material, weather, time-of-day, and heat-emission state, and adapt a pretrained Stable Diffusion backbone to the thermal domain. Because the radiometric content is determined entirely by the prompt, Text2Thermal synthesizes thermal imagery without requiring a registered RGB image at inference; where spatial guidance is desired, an optional control signal imparts scene geometry without disturbing the prompt-specified radiometry. Experiments on M3FD, FLIR, and FMB show that Text2Thermal achieves state-of-the-art FID among thermal image synthesis methods while offering text-level control that translation-based approaches cannot provide.

AI.tldr: A text-conditioned framework, Text2Thermal, translates textual priors into radiometric-consistent thermal imagery using a Stable Diffusion backbone, enabling RGB-free inference and controllable spatial guidance; it achieves state-of-the-art FID on thermal datasets.
AI.motivation: Thermal data are scarce and RGB→thermal translation is ill-posed because emissivity and temperature are not observable in RGB. Language offers a natural disambiguation by specifying material, weather, time-of-day, and heat-emission state.
AI.method: Leverages thermally grounded captions that encode radiometric factors; adapts a pretrained Stable Diffusion model to the thermal domain; radiometric content is set by the prompt; optionally uses a control signal for geometry without altering radiometry; does not require a registered RGB image at inference; evaluates on M3FD, FLIR, and FMB datasets.
AI.result: Text2Thermal achieves state-of-the-art Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) among thermal image synthesis methods and provides text-level control that translation-based methods lack.
AI.conclusion: Language priors can resolve radiometric ambiguity in thermal image synthesis; the proposed text-conditioned framework enables physics-aware, controllable thermal generation without RGB input, improving both realism (FID) and versatility.

title: Inferring Affective Consciousness in an Artificial Agent: A Case Study
summary: Creatures that display 'hedonic place preference behaviour' are thought by many scientists to experience feelings, on the assumption that their attraction to pleasure-producing substances which lack nutritional value (e.g. cocaine, morphine) cannot easily be attributed to unconscious instinctual behaviour. In this paper, we discuss how a simple artificial agent that instantiates attributes of an affective system engaging in felt uncertainty about its intrinsic needs in relation to environmental resources can similarly display hedonic place preference behaviour -- through an apparently subjective form of information processing -- while simultaneously being entirely deter-ministic. We outline some implications of this artificially engineered behaviour for our understanding of the physical basis of consciousness and the experience of free will.

AI.tldr: A deterministic artificial agent with an affective system and intrinsic-need uncertainty can exhibit hedonic place preference behavior, mimicking subjective experience.
AI.motivation: To test whether hedonic place preference requires conscious feelings or could emerge from simple affective processing, challenging assumptions about consciousness and free will.
AI.method: Construct a simple deterministic artificial agent with an affective framework that includes felt uncertainty about intrinsic needs, interacting with environmental resources; observe hedonic place preference behavior as a function of this processing.
AI.result: The agent displays hedonic place preference-like behavior through apparently subjective information processing while remaining fully deterministic.
AI.conclusion: These findings have implications for the physical basis of consciousness and the experience of free will, suggesting hedonic behaviors could be produced without consciousness, informing debates in philosophy of mind and neuroscience.

title: A Two-Stage Forecasting System for CPU Workload Prediction in Private Clouds
summary: Accurate cloud resource forecasting is essential for proactive resource provisioning, maintaining Quality of Service (QoS), and reducing operational costs in dynamic cloud environments. The existing forecasting approaches predominantly estimate future CPU workload directly from historical resource traces, which often overlook the relationship between customer service demand and subsequent resource consumption. This study proposes a two-stage integrated forecasting model that explicitly models this dependency by first forecasting customer service requests, expressed as Transactions Per Second (TPS), and subsequently estimating future CPU workload from the TPS forecast. Both the forecasting component and resource prediction component employed the XGBoost model within a cascaded learning architecture, complemented by adaptive online retraining using an expanding-window strategy to address concept drift in continuously evolving cloud workloads. The proposed work was evaluated using real-world traces collected from a private cloud environment comprising ten applications. Experimental results demonstrate robust forecasting performance by achieving Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) below $7\%$ for most applications, with the best-performing application achieving an MAE of $0.7372$, RMSE of $1.1866$, SMAPE of $3.57\%$, and an R2 of $0.9185$. Horizon-wise drift analysis confirmed stable recursive forecasting behavior with controlled error accumulation across a 60-step prediction horizon. Compared with the conventional direct CPU forecasting method, the proposed two-stage integrated model gives improved forecasting robustness, computational efficiency, and interpretability, making it well-suited for proactive resource management and intelligent auto-scaling in cloud computing environments.

AI.tldr: Two-stage cascaded forecasting: first predict TPS (Transactions Per Second), then infer CPU workload; uses XGBoost with expanding-window online retraining; improves robustness and efficiency for proactive cloud auto-scaling.
AI.motivation: Addresses the mismatch between customer service demand and resource consumption in dynamic cloud environments, by explicitly modeling the dependency from TPS to CPU usage and adapting to concept drift.
AI.method: Two-stage model: stage-1 forecasts TPS; stage-2 forecasts CPU workload from the TPS forecast. Both stages employ XGBoost within a cascaded learning architecture. Online retraining with expanding-window strategy to handle non-stationarity. Evaluated on real traces from a private cloud with ten applications.
AI.result: SMAPE < 7% for most applications; best-case MAE 0.7372, RMSE 1.1866, SMAPE 3.57%, R2 0.9185. Horizon-wise drift analysis shows stable recursive forecasting over a 60-step horizon. Outperforms direct CPU-forecasting in robustness, efficiency, and interpretability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed two-stage integrated model effectively enables proactive resource management and smart auto-scaling in cloud environments by leveraging the TPS→CPU dependency, with strong empirical results and adaptability to concept drift.

title: Catalogue Photography as a Cold Start: Toward Deployable Carbide Burr Recognition
comment: Extended abstract not yet published to a conference or journal
summary: Verifying that manufactured batches of milling tools or carbide rotary burrs conform to production order sheets remains a largely manual and error-prone quality assurance task. Automating this process with computer vision faces a critical cold-start constraint since no labelled imagery is available, leaving manufacturer catalogue photography as the sole source of supervision. We investigate how far catalogue supervision can support an industrial recognition pipeline under domain shift, explicitly measuring the gap between catalogue separability and performance on held-out field photographs. Our findings reveal three key insights. First, off-the-shelf frozen feature extractors do not reliably separate the two task attributes, head shape and tooth profile, motivating targeted representation learning. Second, metric learning produces near-perfect unsupervised cluster discovery on catalogue images (adjusted Rand index 0.94--0.97), but less than half of this gain transfers to field photographs. Third, the largest transfer gains do not come from model scale or representation complexity, but from simple changes that reduce domain sensitivity: converting images to grayscale (+0.22) and constraining retrieval using the known order sheet via Hungarian assignment (+0.11). We therefore treat catalogue photography as a useful cold start rather than a deployment-ready training domain, and provide empirical baselines and an evaluation protocol for catalogue-to-field transfer in precision tool manufacturing.

AI.tldr: Catalogue supervision can bootstrap industrial recognition under domain shift but does not yet reach deployment-ready performance; metric learning yields strong catalogue clustering yet limited transfer to field images; simple domain-sensitivity reductions (grayscale, Hungarian assignment) offer the main transfer gains.
AI.motivation: Automate QA for manufactured milling tools and carbide burrs by verifying conformance to production orders. The lack of labeled field data creates a cold-start problem where catalogue imagery is the primary supervision source, necessitating an understanding of catalogue-to-field transfer under domain shift.
AI.method: Evaluate off-the-shelf frozen feature extractors for separating head shape vs tooth profile; apply metric learning to catalogue images to enable unsupervised clustering; quantify transfer of clustering gains to field photographs; test simple domain-adaptation steps (grayscale conversion, and retrieval constrained by known order via Hungarian assignment); provide an evaluation protocol for catalogue-to-field transfer.
AI.result: Metric learning yields near-perfect unsupervised clusters on catalogue images (adjusted Rand index ~0.94–0.97). Transfer to field photographs is substantially weaker (less than half of catalogue gains transfer). The largest transfer gains come from simple, domain-sensitivity-reducing steps: grayscale conversion (+0.22) and constraining retrieval with Hungarian assignment (+0.11). catalogue photography is a useful cold start but not deployment-ready; the work provides empirical baselines and an evaluation protocol for catalogue-to-field transfer in precision tool manufacturing.
AI.conclusion: Catalogue imagery can seed an industrial recognition pipeline, but bridging the real-world domain gap requires targeted representation learning and likely domain-adaptation strategies beyond model scale or representation complexity. The study offers baselines and a protocol to quantify catalogue-to-field transfer.

title: Lose the Order, Keep the Hierarchy: Deordering HTN Plans
summary: Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning is a powerful planning formalism based on task decomposition. Although most of the literature studied plan generation, comparatively less attention has been paid to post-plan optimization. In particular, plan deordering has been extensively studied in classical planning but remains under-researched in the HTN setting. Plan deordering removes unnecessary ordering constraints between actions in a plan whilst keeping the plan valid. In this paper, we adapt two established plan deordering techniques from classical planning by extending the techniques to account for hierarchical decomposition constraints. We evaluate our proposed approaches on the IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks and we compare them against Optiplan, an HTN planner that generates partially ordered plans directly. Our results show a substantial reduction in number of ordering constraints in both our implementations. Although we also observe a reduction in critical path length, the improvements are less pronounced.

AI.tldr: Extends two classical plan deordering techniques to HTN planning by incorporating hierarchical decomposition constraints; empirically reduces the number of ordering constraints, with modest impact on critical path length, versus Optiplan on IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks.
AI.motivation: HTN planning emphasizes task decomposition, but plan deordering in HTN is under-explored. Reducing unnecessary ordering constraints can yield more flexible and potentially more efficient HTN plans while preserving validity.
AI.method: Adapt two established plan deordering techniques from classical planning to HTN by integrating hierarchical decomposition constraints. Implemented approaches are evaluated on IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks and compared against Optiplan, an HTN planner that directly generates partially ordered plans.
AI.result: Both HTN deordering approaches substantially reduce the number of ordering constraints in the resulting plans. There is also a reduction in the critical path length, though the improvements are less pronounced than for the constraint count.
AI.conclusion: Plan deordering is viable in HTN planning; accounting for hierarchical constraints preserves plan validity while yielding more flexible, less constrained plans. The methods perform well against a direct HTN planner (Optiplan), with stronger gains in constraint reduction than in critical-path improvement.

title: Mind the Gap: Robustness Risks in PII Detection Systems
summary:
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection is a foundational component of data protection infrastructure where missed entities constitute direct privacy and security risks. Although modern PII systems report strong performance on standard benchmarks, we show that these evaluations mask substantial robustness failures under realistic distribution shifts encountered in deployment. Rather than comparing state-of-the-art accuracy, we study how different PII detection paradigms fail under noisy, unstructured, and informal inputs. We construct a stress test benchmark spanning seven categories of natural distribution shift and evaluate representative systems from three widely deployed architectural families: encoder-based NER (SpaCy), rule-based hybrid detection (Presidio), and generative LLM extraction (Qwen2.5-3B).
  All three exhibit significant degradation on out-of-distribution inputs, but with distinct and complementary failure modes. Encoder models primarily fail on unseen surface forms and boundary detection, rule-based systems fail on non-standard formats, and LLMs exhibit entity-type confusion and generation instability. These results show that aggregate benchmark scores obscure deployment-critical weaknesses and that no single architecture is uniformly reliable across PII categories. Motivated by these findings, we propose a hybrid detection pipeline with a QA-driven feedback loop for iterative risk mitigation, and release our benchmark to support OOD-aware evaluation of PII systems.

AI.tldr: PII detection models degrade under distribution shifts; a three-architecture study reveals distinct failure modes; proposes a QA-driven hybrid pipeline and releases an OOD benchmark.
AI.motivation: Deployments face noisy, unstructured inputs and distribution shifts; current benchmarks overestimate robustness; need robust, OOD-aware evaluation for PII systems.
AI.method: Construct a seven-category stress-test benchmark; evaluate encoder-based NER (SpaCy), rule-based hybrid detection (Presidio), and generative LLM extraction (Qwen2.5-3B); analyze failure modes; propose a hybrid pipeline with QA feedback.
AI.result: All three architectures suffer significant performance drops on OOD data; encoder models struggle with unseen surface forms/boundaries, rule-based with non-standard formats, LLMs with entity-type confusion and generation instability.
AI.conclusion: Benchmarking accuracy hides deployment risks; no single architecture is universally reliable; a hybrid, QA-driven risk-mitigation pipeline is proposed; benchmark released for OOD-aware evaluation.

title: Subspace Inference Enables Efficient Active Reward Learning from Preferences
summary: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) has emerged as a powerful yet sample-inefficient approach for learning reward models from human preferences, making active learning a critical component in synthesizing informative preference queries. However, effective uncertainty quantification required for active learning remains a key challenge for large neural network reward models. In this paper, we introduce PreferenceEKF, a sample-efficient approach that tracks reward model uncertainty by framing active preference learning as a sequential Bayesian filtering problem. Instead of relying on computationally prohibitive posterior inference over the full neural network parameter space, our method performs sequential inference via an extended Kalman filter within a low-dimensional parameter subspace, continuously updating the reward model posterior as new preference queries arrive. Our approach enables scalable sampling of neural network parameters to efficiently compute acquisition functions for active reward learning. Experiments on the D4RL and V-D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that our approach achieves better sample efficiency, runtime, scalability, and calibration compared to other Bayesian deep learning approaches, and the learned reward models lead to competitive offline reinforcement learning policy performance. This highlights the potential of scalable Bayesian methods for preference-based reward modeling in RLHF. Our code is available at https://github.com/yutaizhou/bnn_pref.

AI.tldr: PreferenceEKF frames active preference learning as sequential Bayesian filtering, using an extended Kalman filter in a low-dimensional subspace to efficiently quantify reward-model uncertainty for RLHF.
AI.motivation: Uncertainty quantification for active learning with large neural network reward models is sample-inefficient and computationally challenging; a scalable Bayesian approach is needed.
AI.method: Sequential inference via an extended Kalman filter in a reduced parameter subspace; updates the reward-model posterior with each new preference; enables scalable sampling for acquisition functions; supports efficient active reward learning.
AI.result: Improved sample efficiency, runtime, scalability, and calibration versus other Bayesian DL methods on D4RL and V-D4RL benchmarks; learned reward models yield competitive offline RL policy performance.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates the potential of scalable Bayesian methods for preference-based reward modeling in RLHF; code is publicly available.

title: Auditing Patient Privacy in Medical Generative Models: Scalable Memorization Detection with DeepSSIM++
summary: While deep generative models offer new opportunities for medical image synthesis and data sharing, their ability to memorize and reproduce training samples raises serious concerns about patient confidentiality. Detecting such memorization at scale remains challenging: traditional pixel-based metrics are sensitive to generation artifacts, whereas generic embedding-based metrics often lack the anatomical sensitivity required for medical data. To address this challenge, we introduce DeepSSIM++, a self-supervised similarity metric for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative models. By leveraging multi-scale feature aggregation and anatomy-preserving augmentations, DeepSSIM++ learns an embedding space where cosine similarity approximates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), eliminating the need for exact pixel-level registration. Compared with state-of-the-art baselines, DeepSSIM++ achieves an average Macro F1 improvement of 33 percentage points under ideal alignment and 46 percentage points under realistic spatial and intensity perturbations. Furthermore, it accelerates large-scale similarity computation by several orders of magnitude compared with analytical SSIM. By combining anatomical sensitivity and computational efficiency, DeepSSIM++ provides an open-source tool for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative AI. Code and data are publicly available at: https://github.com/brAIn-science/DeepSSIM.

AI.tldr: DeepSSIM++ introduces a self-supervised embedding metric that makes cosine similarity approximate SSIM for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative models by using multi-scale features and anatomy-preserving augmentations; it achieves large gains in Macro F1 over baselines and is computationally efficient, with open-source release.
AI.motivation: Memorization of training data by medical image generative models poses patient privacy risks. Existing metrics are either pixel-sensitive to generation artifacts (pixel-based) or lack anatomical sensitivity (generic embeddings). There is a need for a scalable, anatomically aware, efficient auditing metric.
AI.method: Train a self-supervised embedding space where cosine similarity approximates SSIM using multi-scale feature aggregation and anatomy-preserving augmentations. This avoids pixel-level registration and accelerates large-scale similarity computation. Compare against baselines on memorization detection with a focus on anatomical sensitivity and robustness to spatial/intensity perturbations.
AI.result: DeepSSIM++ outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average Macro F1 improvement of 33 percentage points under ideal alignment and 46 percentage points under realistic perturbations. It also speeds up similarity computation by orders of magnitude versus analytic SSIM, enabling scalable auditing.
AI.conclusion: Anatomically aware, self-supervised embedding metric suitable for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative AI, released as open-source (code and data available).

title: Value-Preserving Architectures for Agentic AI Systems
comment: Accepted to AgenticDev Workshop at ASE 2026
summary: The emergence of agentic AI and LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) presents unprecedented opportunities for automating complex tasks, while simultaneously raising critical concerns about the preservation of fundamental human-centered values, such as privacy, fairness, and safety. Although software engineering has traditionally focused on functional correctness, the adoption of LLMs and AI agents into complex socio-technical systems has intensified the need for responsible software engineering and robust value alignment. In MAS, architectural design decisions, such as coordination mechanisms, communication protocols, and system topologies, play a central role in shaping system behavior and the outcomes they produce. This paper argues that architectural choices influence not only the functionality and performance of MAS but can also promote value-oriented system behavior. Therefore, we investigate how different architectural designs support different human-centered values, discussing the following value-preserving architectural patterns: (i) a privacy-aware architecture with a federated topology, (ii) a distributed architecture to promote pluralism and diversity, and (iii) a guard-agent architecture to detect and mitigate unfairness. Finally, we introduce representative use cases to illustrate the proposed architectures in real-world scenarios. By linking architectural design with human-centered values, this work lays the foundation for a unified set of architectural patterns and guidelines towards the design of trustworthy MAS.

AI.tldr: Value-preserving architectural patterns for trustworthy MAS with LLMs, linking design choices to privacy, diversity, and fairness, and illustrating with use cases.
AI.motivation: Address the need for responsible software engineering and value alignment as MAS and LLM-driven systems become prevalent, recognizing that architectural decisions shape human-centered outcomes.
AI.method: Propose and discuss three value-preserving architectural patterns—privacy-aware federated topology, distributed architecture to promote pluralism/diversity, and guard-agent architecture for unfairness detection/mitigation—and illustrate them with representative use cases.
AI.result: Identification of three architectural patterns and argument that architecture can actively promote human-centered values, providing a foundation for a unified pattern set and guidelines for trustworthy MAS.
AI.conclusion: Architectural design is a lever for value alignment in MAS; the work lays groundwork for pattern-based guidelines and further empirical validation and tooling.

title: Spectral characteristics of autoencoder parameters as a vector representation of data
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures. This is a shortened (theorem proofs are skipped) and translated version of the paper published in a Russian-language peer-reviewed journal, the citation is in the paper footnote
summary: This paper examines the relationship between the parameters of autoencoder models and the statistical properties of the data on which they are trained. Autoencoders are defined as models with an encoder-decoder architecture, trained to reconstruct input data through a compressed latent representation. It is proposed that the model parameters can be viewed as a dense vector representation of the corresponding sample. To test this hypothesis, a theoretical and experimental study is conducted in which a vector representation is formed based on the spectral characteristics of the autoencoder parameter matrices. Theoretical analysis shows that the singular values of the model parameter matrices are related to the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix of the training data, ensuring the transfer of information between the data space and the parameter space. Experimental results on the CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST datasets confirm that the resulting vector representations allow for a high degree of accuracy in distinguishing between models trained on different data subsets, without resorting to complex vector generation algorithms or using the original samples. These results suggest that the parameters of trained autoencoders can be viewed as sample representations.

AI.tldr: Autoencoder parameters serve as sample representations; singular values of parameter matrices reflect data covariance eigenvalues; spectral features enable distinguishing models trained on different data subsets; validated on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST.
AI.motivation: To determine whether trained autoencoder parameters encode information about the training data and can act as compact representations of samples, linking data statistics to parameter space via spectral properties.
AI.method: Form vector representations from the spectral characteristics (singular values) of autoencoder parameter matrices; establish theoretically that these singular values relate to the covariance eigenvalues of training data; empirically test on CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST by classifying or clustering models trained on different data subsets using these vectors.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis shows singular values relate to data covariance eigenvalues, enabling information transfer between data and parameter spaces; spectral vectors differentiate models trained on different data subsets with high accuracy; no reliance on original samples or complex generation methods.
AI.conclusion: Autoencoder parameters can be viewed as sample representations; spectral-based vectorization captures data statistics and enables effective model comparison and dataset fingerprinting.

title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: Bridging the gap between the discrete reasoning of Vision-Language Models and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce LaPla, a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework featuring latent-aligned planning to seamlessly ground semantic understanding in precise motion execution. We first design an action tokenizer based on a residual vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), capturing vehicle kinematics and encoding trajectory features into a structured latent space. Rather than discrete codebook lookups that inevitably introduce quantization errors, LaPla repurposes this representation as a physical prior to bridge the modality gap between high-dimensional semantics and the raw action space. Specifically, given multimodal inputs integrating multi-view images, historical actions, and textual instructions, LaPla incorporates concurrent action queries to causally attend to the multimodal context in a single forward pass, projecting hidden states directly into the pretrained VQ-VAE latent space. The frozen decoder then translates these continuous latents into actions, effectively eliminating quantization errors and ensuring physically plausible trajectories while bypassing time-consuming autoregressive generation. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that LaPla achieves competitive open-loop performance, reducing long-horizon L2 error by 15.52% compared to state-of-the-art VLA methods. Closed-loop evaluations on the NVIDIA AlpaSim simulator further confirm its superior capability in ensuring smooth driving progress, improving the success rate by 33.34 percentage points with significantly reduced inference latency.

AI.tldr: LaPla introduces a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework that uses a residual vector-quantized VQ-VAE as an action tokenizer. By projecting multimodal inputs into the VQ-VAE latent space and using a frozen decoder, it provides single-pass, physically plausible actions without quantization errors, achieving state-of-the-art-like improvements in open-loop and closed-loop autonomous driving benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Bridge the gap between discrete, language-driven reasoning in vision-language models and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving; reduce quantization and latency while maintaining physical plausibility.
AI.method: Design a residual vector-quantized VAE to encode trajectory features into a latent space; map multimodal inputs (images, history, text) into this latent space via concurrent action queries; use a frozen VQ-VAE decoder to generate continuous actions, avoiding autoregressive generation and quantization errors.
AI.result: NuScenes open-loop: long-horizon L2 error reduced by 15.52% relative to state-of-the-art VLA methods. NVIDIA AlpaSim closed-loop: success rate improved by 33.34 percentage points with lower inference latency.
AI.conclusion: Latent-aligned planning with a VQ-VAE latent space provides a physically grounded, efficient bridge between semantic understanding and motion execution, yielding improved open- and closed-loop driving performance while avoiding common quantization and slow generation pitfalls.

title: EraseSAE: Surgical Concept Erasure in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Recent advances in text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable generative capabilities, yet their reliance on loosely curated training data raises pressing safety and copyright concerns. Concept erasure offers a principled remedy by removing unwanted semantics from pretrained models while preserving remaining concepts. However, existing approaches typically operate at a coarse granularity misaligned with the fine-grained, distributed nature of concept representations, leading to incomplete removal or degraded generation quality. We argue that surgical erasure fundamentally requires intervention at the level of monosemantic features, where each unit encodes a single interpretable concept. To this end, we propose EraseSAE, a novel framework that leverages sparse autoencoders to achieve surgical concept erasure in DiT-based T2V diffusion models via a principled decompose-attribute-erase pipeline. We first introduce the Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder, which decomposes dense spatiotemporal activations into disentangled, interpretable sparse features while preserving spatiotemporal coherence. A contrastive attribution mechanism then contrasts activations from paired prompts to isolate concept-specific feature kernels. At inference, timestep-resolved spatiotemporal masks derived from the identified kernels confine erasure to regions where the target concept is active, leaving unrelated content intact. Extensive experiments across diverse diffusion models and concept erasure tasks demonstrate that EraseSAE achieves precise and robust concept removal with minimal quality degradation, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/HiDream-ai/EraseSAE.

AI.tldr: EraseSAE introduces a surgical concept erasure for text-to-video diffusion via a Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder. It decomposes activations into monosemantic, disentangled features, identifies concept-specific kernels using contrastive attribution, and applies timestep-resolved masks to erase target concepts while preserving rest; outperforms prior methods.
AI.motivation: Safety and copyright concerns due to data-driven generation in T2V models; need fine-grained, unit-level concept erasure rather than coarse granularity.
AI.method: Propose Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder (P-CSA) to decompose dense spatiotemporal activations into sparse, interpretable features; use contrastive attribution across paired prompts to isolate concept-specific kernels; inference uses masks to confine erasure to active regions across time.
AI.result: Comprehensive experiments across diffusion models and erasure tasks show precise, robust removal with minimal quality loss; outperforms state-of-the-art; code released.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of monosemantic surgical erasure in T2V models; EraseSAE preserves content elsewhere, enabling safer, copyright-compliant generation; scalable, though may incur computational overhead and rely on paired prompts.

title: Speak for Me: Giving LLMs the Situational Awareness to Participate in a Meeting
summary: In online meeting delegation, LLM agents fail to recognize when to speak. With no structured way to track stances, coverage, and floor, they miss the moments where they should contribute. Prompt-only delegates stay silent on 51.4% of the absent participant's talking opportunities on the AMI corpus. We present CAPA (Collaborative Agent Predictive Architecture), an architecture for online meeting delegation. A Perceiver updates the meeting state from each observed turn. A Predictor forecasts how the conversation will continue. A Controller decides whether to speak and which proposition to surface. A Generator phrases the chosen contribution in the participant's style. Two judges score the forecast and the action against the next observed turn. A Recalibrator updates the meeting state from those verdicts for future decisions. To evaluate online delegation, we introduce an episode-level protocol that scores whether, when, and what a delegate contributes around the participant's actual idea units. The protocol's schema-constrained LLM judges align with human annotations at Cohen's kappa = 0.71. On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces the silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1 --> 52.2), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with each residual near-miss attributable to a specific module of the architecture. Mechanism ablations identify the meeting state as the lever that closes the recognition gap, where raw-context scaling alone does not.

AI.tldr: CAPA enables online meeting delegates to contribute reliably via a structured agent stack that tracks meeting state, forecasts dialogue, selects and surfaces contributions, and updates state based on judgments; evaluated on AMI with substantial reductions in silence and maintained low hallucination.
AI.motivation: Prompt-only LLM delegates miss speaking opportunities due to lack of structured tracking of stance, coverage, and floor in real-time meetings (AMI). A formal architecture is needed to coordinate when and what to contribute.
AI.method: CAPA comprises: (1) Perceiver updates meeting state from each observed turn; (2) Predictor forecasts how the conversation will continue; (3) Controller decides whether to speak and selects a proposition; (4) Generator phrases the chosen contribution in the participant's style; (5) Two judges score the forecast and action against the next observed turn; (6) Recalibrator updates the meeting state from verdicts for future decisions. Evaluation uses an episode-level protocol with schema-constrained LLM judges aligning with human annotations (Cohen’s kappa = 0.71).
AI.result: On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces the silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1% → 52.2%), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with residual near-misses tied to specific modules. Mechanism ablations show the meeting state as the lever to close the recognition gap; raw-context scaling alone is insufficient.
AI.conclusion: Explicit meeting-state modeling (CAPA) effectively closes the recognition gap in online delegation, with modular components enabling targeted improvements; ablations highlight the meeting state as the key lever and identify residual errors to guide future refinements.

title: Restricted Eigenvalues Beyond Gaussian Width: Threshold Occupancy under Heavy Tails
summary: Restricted eigenvalue (RE) bounds govern stable recovery by norm-regularized estimators. For isotropic sub-Gaussian measurements, the benchmark sample size is $1+w(A)^2$, where $w(A)$ is the Gaussian width of the normalized descent cone. The COLT 2015 open-problem note (Banerjee et al., 2015) asked whether the same law follows for heavy-tailed designs from a uniform small-ball condition alone. We give an explicit and systematic negative answer to the general question as formulated there: the proposed law fails in its full dimension-free, arbitrary-set form, and the missing obstruction is simultaneous threshold occupancy. A constant-width polyhedral descent cone with fixed small-ball constants has zero empirical RE on every sample path up to half the ambient dimension. More generally, every finite range space admits exact threshold encoding in an arbitrarily narrow spherical cap and a lift to a full polyhedral descent-cone section. For every fixed threshold VC dimension $d$, as $β\downarrow0$, the sharp worst-case sample complexity is $Θ(β^{-1}[d\log(1/β)+\log(1/δ)])$. The separation persists under exact isotropy and all finite moments: on the same constant-width cone, Gaussian measurements succeed with $O(1+\log(1/δ))$ samples, whereas an isotropic heavy-tailed design fails pathwise for $n\lesssim\sqrt{p/\log p}$. Gaussian smoothing yields an everywhere-positive $C^\infty$ density while retaining arbitrarily poor RE. Under isotropy, a distribution-free fallback governed by affine dimension times squared enclosing radius is sharp on this family.

AI.tldr: Heavy-tailed designs invalidates the universal RE bound n ~ 1+w(A)^2 that holds for isotropic sub-Gaussians. The COLT 2015 open problem is answered in the negative: a fixed-width, polyhedral descent cone with bounded small-ball constants has zero empirical RE on all sample paths up to about half the ambient dimension; threshold encoding via VC-dimension yields a dimension-dependent worst-case sample complexity Θ(β^{-1}[d log(1/β)+log(1/δ)]) for fixed d. Gaussian designs separate: they achieve O(1+log(1/δ)) samples while isotropic heavy-tailed designs fail pathwise for n ≲ √(p/ log p). Gaussian smoothing improves density but preserves poor RE. A distribution-free fallback under isotropy scales with affine dimension times squared enclosing radius.
AI.motivation: Clarify whether the heavy-tailed design RE behavior matches the Gaussian/sub-Gaussian case under a uniform small-ball condition and resolve whether a dimension-free law exists for general descent cones.
AI.method: Construct explicit counterexamples using constant-width polyhedral descent cones; encode finite range spaces via threshold occupancy in narrow spherical caps; analyze worst-case sample complexity through VC-dimension d and threshold β, derive θ(β^{-1}[d log(1/β)+log(1/δ)]) scaling; compare heavy-tailed vs Gaussian performance under exact isotropy and finite moments; examine smoothing effects on density and RE.
AI.result: Disproof of the universal dimension-free RE law for heavy-tailed designs. There exist cones and designs with zero empirical RE up to n ≈ p/2; for fixed VC-dimension d, worst-case sample complexity is Θ(β^{-1}[d log(1/β)+log(1/δ)]) as β→0. Gaussian measurements recover RE with O(1+log(1/δ)) samples; heavy-tailed, isotropic designs fail pathwise for n ≲ √(p/log p). Gaussian smoothing yields a positive density yet does not cure poor RE; a dimension-free, distribution-free bound is governed instead by affine dimension and squared enclosing radius.
AI.conclusion: RE-based guarantees are not universally robust to heavy-tailed designs. The obstruction is simultaneous threshold occupancy. Practical implication: one must consider dimension- and threshold-structure (VC-dimension) when extending RE-based guarantees beyond Gaussian-like designs; Gaussian designs remain superior under the same small-ball constants.

title: A Low-Cost, Open Platform for End-to-End Autonomous Driving on a Miniature Ackermann Vehicle
summary: This paper presents a low-cost, open experimental platform for research in end-to-end autonomous driving with miniature Ackermann vehicles. The platform combines a physical vehicle, a printed urban track, data collection tools, trajectory registration, and a Webots digital twin, enabling controlled experiments that connect simulation-based autonomous-driving methods to real-world execution. As a first baseline, we implement command-conditioned behavior cloning, in which a neural policy receives an on-board camera image and a high-level navigation command and outputs steering and speed. The system is evaluated both on the physical vehicle and in simulation. In real closed-loop experiments, the learned policy follows lanes and executes commanded turns, reaching a mean cross-track error of 6.1 cm with respect to the reference route, close to the 4.7 cm observed in human demonstrations. In the digital twin, camera field of view has a strong effect on performance, reducing the mean cross-track error from 35.6 to 3.3 cm when widened from 58 to 120 degrees. Using the digital twin to generate synthetic driving data and a learned sim-to-real image translator to reduce the appearance gap, we further show that a higher-capacity policy trained on this synthetic data combined with real demonstrations is the only configuration that completes all four track routes in closed loop, whereas the compact baseline and the same network trained on real data alone complete fewer. These results establish the open platform as a practical testbed for sim-to-real studies and provide an initial command-conditioned imitation-learning baseline; we release it to support reproducible research.

AI.tldr: Open, low-cost end-to-end autonomous-driving platform using miniature Ackermann vehicles with a digital twin and sim-to-real data strategy; baseline imitation learning; results show notable impact of camera FOV and synthetic data on performance.
AI.motivation: Provide a reproducible, accessible testbed that links simulation-based autonomous-driving methods to real-world execution, addressing sim-to-real gaps and enabling controlled experiments on a scalable platform.
AI.method: Hardware platform (miniature Ackermann vehicle, printed urban track, data tools, trajectory registration) plus Webots digital twin; baseline command-conditioned behavior cloning using on-board camera and high-level commands to produce steering/speed; evaluation in real vehicle and simulation; systematic study of camera field of view; synthetic data generation via digital twin with a learned sim-to-real image translator; higher-capacity policy trained on synthetic+real data evaluated on four track routes.
AI.result: Real-world closed-loop: mean cross-track error (CTE) 6.1 cm, near human 4.7 cm. Digital twin: increasing camera FOV from 58° to 120° reduces CTE from 35.6 cm to 3.3 cm. Higher-capacity policy trained on synthetic+real data completes all four tracks in closed loop, whereas baseline models trained on real data alone fail on some tracks.
AI.conclusion: The open platform is a practical, reproducible testbed for sim-to-real research in autonomous driving; the study provides a baseline imitation-learning approach and demonstrates the benefits of larger FOV and synthetic data with a real-to-sim translator for bridging sim-to-real gaps.

title: Stabilizing Camera-Controlled Novel View Synthesis at Inference Time
summary: Training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from a single image using pre-trained video diffusion models often becomes unstable under large camera motion and long generation horizons. Existing approaches commonly combine several inference-time components, making it unclear which design choices are most important for stability. We show that the main source of stability is simple. Decomposing camera motion into small autoregressive steps limits per-step geometric distortion and reduces error accumulation. A controlled camera-step study shows that performance remains stable for small motions and degrades more strongly as the per-step motion approaches $18$-$20^\circ$. We further evaluate geometry-constrained spatial attention and low-frequency appearance anchoring as supporting refinements, together with an efficient registration-free warping pipeline. Across RealEstate10K and MegaScene, CamTrol++ improves temporal and geometric consistency, downstream 3D reconstruction quality, and generation efficiency over training-free baselines. The method remains effective for 56-frame generation and under substantial controlled depth corruption. These results show that careful control of camera motion at inference time can substantially improve the stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis without retraining or modifying the diffusion backbone.

AI.tldr: Autoregressive, small-camera-motion decomposition improves stability in training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from a single image using pre-trained video diffusion models; CamTrol++ with geometry constraints and low-frequency anchoring achieves better temporal/geometric consistency and 3D reconstruction without retraining.
AI.motivation: Stability issues under large camera motion and long generation horizons in training-free NVS; identify design choices that most influence stability without retraining the diffusion backbone.
AI.method: Decompose camera motion into small autoregressive steps to limit per-step distortion; controlled camera-step study showing stability for small motions and degradation near 18–20 degrees; add geometry-constrained spatial attention and low-frequency appearance anchoring; efficient registration-free warping; evaluate on RealEstate10K and MegaScene; test up to 56-frame generation and in presence of depth corruption.
AI.result: CamTrol++ improves temporal and geometric consistency, downstream 3D reconstruction quality, and generation efficiency over training-free baselines; robust across 56-frame generation and substantial depth corruption.
AI.conclusion: Careful inference-time control of camera motion substantially improves stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis without retraining or backbone modification.

title: Towards Numerical TOHTN Planning with SMT-based HTN-SAT Encoding
summary: While HTN planning has received significant attention in recent years, support for numerical reasoning remains very limited. In this paper, we investigate numerical Totally-Ordered HTN (TOHTN) planning and show how standard SAT-based encodings can be naturally extended with SMT to handle numeric fluents. In addition, we introduce a benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN planning, providing a first common basis for evaluation in this setting. Experimental results show that this simple encoding already constitutes a competitive baseline. This work opens the way to more expressive approaches to HTN planning.

AI.tldr: Extends SAT-based HTN encodings with SMT to support numerical TOHTN planning, introduces a benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN, and shows competitive baseline results, indicating a path toward more expressive HTN planning.
AI.motivation: HTN planning often lacks robust support for numerical reasoning; there is a need for numerical TOHTN planning and standardized evaluation benchmarks.
AI.method: Develop a numerical TOHTN framework by integrating SMT for numeric fluents into SAT-based encodings; create a benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN planning to enable standardized evaluation.
AI.result: The proposed encoding is already a competitive baseline according to experimental results.
AI.conclusion: This work enables more expressive HTN planning and suggests future directions for incorporating richer numerical reasoning in HTN planners.

title: An Adversarial Zero-Shot Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate IoT Traffic Data
summary: Anomaly detection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks presents unique challenges due to the diversity of devices, lack of labeled data, and domain variability across environments. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection that leverages adversarial learning and contrastive loss within a sequence-based Variational Autoencoder (VAE) architecture. Our method enables zero-shot domain adaptation by jointly optimizing domain-invariant latent representations and semantically structured embedding spaces, without requiring labeled data or raw feature transfer. To address the heterogeneity of IoT deployments, we introduce encoder and decoder adaptor layers that align feature distributions across domains while preserving contextual semantics.
